title: One orange. Six ways of seeing.
method: Built-in image_gen. AI interpretations of material processes, not physical prints or period artifacts. No separate metered API backend used.
brief: An adult peeling an orange at a kitchen table, with a blue bowl and an open window.
consistency: Initial studies; continuity across unrelated subjects has not yet been tested.

studies.name: The searching line
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create a standalone square illustration for a visual-language study. Shared subject: an ordinary adult with short dark hair, wearing a loose work shirt, seated at a small kitchen table, quietly peeling an orange by hand; one long curling strip of peel, a simple blue bowl on the table, and one open square window. The person is absorbed in the small task, with no smile toward the viewer. No knife. The same scene will be explored in different media; this image must commit to ONE specific material language. An original composition, not a copy of any artist. No lettering, signature, logos, labels or mockup. Show the art itself straight-on and filling the square, not photographed paper on a desk.
Style/medium: a spare drypoint impression on clean pale ivory rag paper. Everything is made from scratched black lines: fine wiry searching contours, occasional heavy velvety burr at a changed direction, small knots of irregular crosshatching. A line is allowed to stop before an outline closes. No filled flat shapes, no washes, no color; even the orange and blue bowl are represented only in black ink. Let three lightly contradictory marks remain around the cheek and wrist, as observation rather than cartoon wobble. The face should feel specifically observed, middle-aged and tired around the eyes, drawn with very few unequal strokes. The chair and lower torso are mostly omitted. About two thirds of the image remains completely unprinted; the open window is suggested by only two unjoined lines. Intimate close composition with head and working hands offset toward the lower right; the long orange peel supplies the loose visual counterline. Shading is local and sparse, not an all-over field of hatch. The needle, ink and pressure determine the edges. Avoid generalized distressed paper, sepia, perfect vector contours, symmetrical hatching, cute cartoon features, decorative border, photorealistic rendering.

studies.name: Colour through a hole
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create a standalone square illustration for a visual-language study. Shared subject: an ordinary adult with short dark hair, wearing a loose work shirt, seated at a small kitchen table, quietly peeling an orange by hand; one long curling strip of peel, a simple blue bowl on the table, and one open square window. The person is absorbed in the small task, with no smile toward the viewer. No knife. The same scene will be explored in different media; this image must commit to ONE specific material language. An original composition, not a copy of any artist. No lettering, signature, logos, labels or mockup. Show the art itself straight-on and filling the square, not photographed paper on a desk.
Style/medium: an original pochoir-inspired illustration constructed from only SIX opaque gouache stencil shapes, with minimal small details cut into those shapes. Saturated ultramarine, rusty vermilion, muted pale green and untouched warm white paper. The person, curved arms, table, bowl and window interlock into a flat asymmetric composition like a compact 1920s decorative-art plate, but the person is an ordinary contemporary adult with an individual crooked profile. Absolutely no drawn outlines and no black ink keyline. Use the geometry of the stencil openings to invent the figure: one angular nose, a solid bent sleeve, bare paper for the hand's interior. A narrow vermilion spiral establishes the peel. Edges have the occasional soft stipple where pigment was pushed through a stencil, while large interiors are firm and opaque. Shadows are a single adjacent color plane, never rendered tonal modelling. Cropped tabletop rising diagonally from lower left; the open square window sits high right. Graphic force and peculiar silhouette take precedence over correct perspective. No antiqued or yellowed overlay, fake age spots, Art Deco lettering, ornamental pattern, gradients, beige-on-beige palette, 3D effect, decorative frame.

studies.name: Light taken out
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create a standalone square illustration for a visual-language study. Shared subject: an ordinary adult with short dark hair, wearing a loose work shirt, seated at a small kitchen table, quietly peeling an orange by hand; one long curling strip of peel, a simple blue bowl on the table, and one open square window. The person is absorbed in the small task, with no smile toward the viewer. No knife. The same scene will be explored in different media; this image must commit to ONE specific material language. An original composition, not a copy of any artist. No lettering, signature, logos, labels or mockup. Show the art itself straight-on and filling the square, not photographed paper on a desk.
Style/medium: a dark-field monotype impression, inked in deep indigo-black on an unworked smooth plate, then LIGHT REMOVED with a rag, a fingertip and a few decisive wipes. The whole scene emerges from two or three broad dark ink masses and luminous wiped paper. No contour drawing and no crosshatching. The window is a bright imperfect rectangular wipe, the face is an oblique pale wedge, the forearms are two broad swiped curves. Retain the directional sweep of the rag and occasional ink dragged at the end of a wipe. The fingers and peel should be understood by a tiny clear negative-space gesture, not individually rendered. One small ochre-orange dab for the fruit and peel; the bowl is a dark blue mass, almost lost against the table. Close, off-centre, late-evening composition, figure low on left, very broad area of uninterrupted blue-black toward upper left and a stark window toward upper right. Tender but unsentimental; a presence in a room, not a glamorous portrait. Let one shoulder merge into the background. The surface must be explained by ink transfer and subtraction; do not sprinkle random scratches or fake stains. No oil-paint bristle impasto, soft digital airbrush, cinematic glow, photographic room detail, decorative speckles, vignette, antique paper border.

studies.name: The scissors decide
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create a standalone square illustration for a visual-language study. Shared subject: an ordinary adult with short dark hair, wearing a loose work shirt, seated at a small kitchen table, quietly peeling an orange by hand; one long curling strip of peel, a simple blue bowl on the table, and one open square window. The person is absorbed in the small task, with no smile toward the viewer. No knife. The same scene will be explored in different media; this image must commit to ONE specific material language. An original composition, not a copy of any artist. No lettering, signature, logos, labels or mockup. Show the art itself straight-on and filling the square, not photographed paper on a desk.
Style/medium: an original bold editorial image assembled from eight to twelve pieces of plain colored paper, cut directly with large scissors without a preliminary drawing. The palette is sharp cobalt blue, tomato red, pale butter yellow, ordinary brown kraft and clean white. Flat overhead reproduction; the cut edges themselves form every contour. Broad cuts make abrupt changes of direction; the profile is unusually long and the shoulders lopsided. One little wedge of white makes the eye, not a drawn dot. Hands are two mitten-like shapes meeting around the orange, with only the indispensable thumb notches, no false extra fingers. The curling peel is a single narrow irregular red-orange ribbon that nearly touches the lower edge. The open window is two disconnected blue rectangles, the bowl a blunt semicircle. Make the seated person and table interlock, and let a gap of uncut white stand for a whole sleeve. Leave one unexpected large triangular empty area. Visible occasional paper fibres only at cut edges; slight color variability of real paper; no drawn lines whatsoever. The humor comes from brave ungainly shape decisions. No drop shadows, layered craft-photography depth, gradients, uniform rounded vector shapes, paper confetti, childish smile, texture overlay, perfect symmetry, decorative frame.

studies.editPrompt: Edit this cut-paper illustration. Preserve the seated adult's main blue-shirt silhouette, hands peeling the orange, long red-orange peel, blue bowl, brown tabletop and the sharp cobalt/tomato/kraft/white material palette. Make a much more radical, simpler editorial composition. REMOVE the entire pendant lamp, plant and vase, landscape, building, tree, sun, floor/rug and visible table legs: those areas become perfectly blank clean white paper. Reduce the window to just ONE detached cobalt quadrilateral high right; no view through it. Keep only a hint of the red chair. Remove the figure's far eye and simplify the near eye to a tiny triangular white cut. Crop the lower body into a single kraft trapezoid. Count roughly twelve large cut shapes total; essential uncut white gaps do most of the work. Refuse realistic modelling or decorative additions. The long orange peel is the only restless small shape, continuing almost to the bottom. Keep a full white margin at right and a large irregular white void between figure and lone window fragment. Direct scissor edges, large slightly awkward cuts, no drawn outlines, no drop shadows. Do not add new objects. Original image is the edit target, not a style reference.

studies.name: Scratch back to colour
studies.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create a standalone square illustration for a visual-language study. Shared subject: an ordinary adult with short dark hair, wearing a loose work shirt, seated at a small kitchen table, quietly peeling an orange by hand; one long curling strip of peel, a simple blue bowl on the table, and one open square window. The person is absorbed in the small task, with no smile toward the viewer. No knife. The same scene will be explored in different media; this image must commit to ONE specific material language. An original composition, not a copy of any artist. No lettering, signature, logos, labels or mockup. Show the art itself straight-on and filling the square, not photographed paper on a desk.
Style/medium: forceful waxy oil pastel with sgraffito on ordinary white cartridge paper. First broad patches of acidic lemon, salmon pink and vivid blue; a heavy dark aubergine pastel layer covers selected parts; a blunt wooden tool scratches through it to reveal colored underlayers. Differentiate broad compressed waxy strokes from the narrow scraped marks and crumbly exposed paper. Those scratches CONSTRUCT the image: the elbow, jaw, window hinge and peel are incised into the dark, rather than decorated afterwards. Thick lateral strokes make the table. The face is an awkward warm pink wedge with one decisive blue eye stroke, and the hair a dark aubergine clump. The orange is small and intensely orange, bowl a bruised blue oval. Compressed shallow space, face high left, hands low centre, window cropped off the upper right edge. Uneven pressure creates broken coverage in some strokes and thick opaque coverage in others. Keep large areas of unmarked white between blunt marks. Energetic and adult, dry and direct, with a slightly uncomfortable color relationship. No soft blending, digital glow, clean contour around every form, evenly distributed grain, cheerful children's-book prettiness, pastel rainbow harmony, decorative border.

studies.name: Carbon & citrus
studies.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create an original square experimental editorial illustration. The scene is an ordinary adult quietly peeling an orange at a small kitchen table, one continuous curling peel, one bowl and the suggestion of an open square window. Invent a personal visual grammar from EXHAUSTED BLUE CARBON PAPER TRANSFER plus a single opaque vermilion-orange stencil. This is a drawing whose authority comes from omission. At least 80 percent of the square must be untouched clean white, not cream or aged paper. The adult is an older heavy-set woman with a blunt short haircut, in plain modern clothes, asymmetrical and absorbed, with no glamour and no smile to the viewer. Put her high toward the left, deliberately crop the top of her head; one oversized working hand and the orange occupy the centre, the right half of the page is almost empty. Describe the whole person and table with fewer than twenty irregular ultramarine-blue line segments. These are pressure-transferred lines, sometimes double-tracked, abruptly broken by poor transfer, indented but not shaded; no hatching or filled skin. Do not complete any enclosing silhouette. A cheek is two strokes, a nose is a wrong-angled little hook, the far eye is completely absent. A single flat orange disk interrupted by a crooked white thumb-notch, and an awkward orange zigzag peel, are the ONLY solid color. The bowl is two disconnected blue arcs at lower right. One unjoined blue corner suggests the window. Hands are readable through the position of a thumb and two pressure lines, not anatomically described. A faint near-miss line beside the wrist is retained. The contrast between fragile incomplete navy drawing and the solid orange fruit is the entire idea. Make a striking severe adult literary-magazine image that can carry a whole page without filling it. No other objects, no potted plants, no landscape, no decorative marks, no lettering, no frames, no paper stains, no background wash, no smooth vector curves, no realistic portrait, no pencil shading, no all-over grain, no 'hand-drawn' uniform wobble. Show the flat art itself, not a mockup.
